notes:
Summary: Lost to hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock). Opportunity stalled in procurement after security and procurement sided with existing AWS relationship.

Key context / shorthand:
- Company: mid-size retail analytics + personalization startup; heavy AWS footprint (EKS, RDS, Cognito, KMS). Already on long-term AWS committed spend.
- Initial ask: replace slower personalization microservice + consolidate embeddings store. Wanted VPC + KMS + per-tenant audit logs.
- Primary use-cases: real-time product personalization (low latency), support bot for returns, offline reranking for recommendations. Expected steady QPS ~200-400 req/s during peak.
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for personalization calls. Cost sensitivity: moderate-high (unit economics matter).

Timeline (bulleted):
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (Jordan/JB). High-level scope, buyer champion identified (Sr. Eng PM: Carla Mendes).
- 2025-11-20: Tech deep-dive w/ Priya (SE) + Eng infra. Discussed VPC private control plane option.
- 2025-12-08: NDA signed; POC scope agreed (hosted-api demo + dedicated staging cluster + KV cache test).
- 2025-12-20: POC kickoff. Provided sample dataset (anonymized catalog + session traces).
- 2026-01-15: Interim POC results: Redwood latency good vs baseline; batching and prefix caching reduced token cost 18%. Eng team impressed with perf.
- 2026-01-22: Security review call (fireflies ff_2026-01-22_4312) — security flagged integration pain: Redwood control plane outside AWS, IAM mapping via SAML could be done but heavier than cloud-native.
- 2026-01-30: Procurement asked for side-by-side TCO with Bedrock/Vertex. We provided cost model + drive deck (drive:/decks/beacon-retail-redwood-poc-deck-v3.pdf).
- 2026-02-04: Final decision call (fireflies ff_2026-02-04_7890) — they chose AWS Bedrock managed endpoints citing consolidated billing, single-vendor SLAs, and simpler IAM + secrets integration.

Quotes / snippets captured:
- "We love the latency numbers, but our security team is pushing for everything to be inside our AWS org — fewer cross-account artifacts." — Carla Mendes (Sr. Eng PM)
- "Procurement says it's easier to justify expansion against existing AWS committed spend." — CFO (procurement thread).

Why lost (concise):
- Hyperscaler lock-in decision driven by existing AWS spend and perceived ops simplicity.
- Security team preferred cloud-native IAM & KMS integration over a separate control plane.
- No strong internal champion after Carla moved to a different initiative; engagement weakened.
- Budget window closed for FY26 Q1; procurement opted for in-cloud managed endpoints as lower short-term friction.

What we pitched and where we won:
- Pitched dedicated + VPC private control plane and on-prem option for data residency. Deliverable POC showed better latency and cost savings at scale vs their baseline.
- Technical stakeholders (ML infra) acknowledged Redwood's runtime advantages: KV caching, quantization guidance, predictable throughput.

Open/next actions (CRM):
- Mark opportunity closed-lost. Record lessons learned: emphasize easier IAM/KMS integrations for future mid-market AWS-first accounts.
- Follow-up cadence: 6 months check-in to discuss migration pain points and cross-cloud strategy (target July 2026).
- Action item: send one-pager on hybrid control-plane patterns and a short checklist for "migrating from hyperscaler endpoints" to rekindle interest when they experience limits. (Drive draft: drive:/sales/onepagers/hybrid-control-plane-checklist.pdf).

Attachments / artifacts: POC deck, security Q&A doc, pricing model spreadsheet (links above).

Notes tone: terse, bullet-heavy (CRM-style). Follow-up recommended but low probability in next quarter.
